\[
w(p, q) \le \min\Big(\operatorname{Int}(C_1) + \frac{k}{\lvert C_1 \rvert},\ \operatorname{Int}(C_2) + \frac{k}{\lvert C_2 \rvert}\Big),
\qquad
k = 1
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(w(p, q)\): The color distance between neighbors p and q
- \(\operatorname{Int}(C)\): The heaviest edge of the minimum spanning tree of region C
- \(k\): The scale

Each pixel is a node, linked to its 8 neighbors by an edge. Its weight w is the color distance after the blur. The edges are taken from the lightest. An edge between two regions C_1 and C_2 joins them when its weight passes a test for both regions. It must be no larger than the internal difference Int of the region plus k over its size. Int(C) is the heaviest edge of the minimum spanning tree of C, the largest step needed to cross it. The term k / |C| lets small regions merge across larger steps. Large regions need a clear boundary to stay apart. Here scikit-image divides the scale by 255, so k works as on pixel levels from 0 to 255.
